query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Minor alloying of equiatomic CoCrFeNi with ~5 at.% Ag will promote self-lubricating Ag-rich tribofilms that keep the coefficient of friction (CoF) below 0.30 and cut the wear rate by ≥50 % from room temperature (25 °C) up to 800 °C in dry air sliding, whereas the undoped CoCrFeNi shows CoF ≥0.45 and higher wear at the same conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted, homogenised, single-phase FCC CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy pins (Ø 4 mm) with average equiaxed grains (~50 µm) and hardness ≈ 200–220 HV.
generation.intervention: Add 5 at.% Ag to form a nominal CoCrFeNiAg0.05 bulk alloy produced by the same melting and homogenisation schedule.
generation.conditions: Unlubricated ball-on-disk sliding in laboratory air (≈40 % RH, 0.1 m s⁻¹), normal load 5 N (Hertzian contact pressure ≤1 GPa), temperatures 25, 400, 600 and 800 °C, sliding distance 1000 m against an Al2O3 counter-body.
generation.structural_mediator: Ag-rich segregated surface/tribofilm layer (≈5–50 nm) sometimes containing soft Ag2O or Ag–Cr mixed oxides atop a nanocrystalline FCC matrix subsurface.
generation.mechanism: Frictional heating and plastic shear drive rapid Ag diffusion/segregation to the contact, where its low shear strength (and, at high T, partial surface melting) provides easy interfacial sliding. Concurrent Ag-Cr-O glaze limits further oxidation and spalls, jointly lowering shear stress and protecting the substrate, hence reducing both CoF and wear across the full temperature span.
generation.predicted_outcome: Mean steady-state CoF 0.20–0.30 at all test temperatures; specific wear rate ≤ 2 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹, roughly half that of the baseline alloy which exhibits CoF 0.45–0.80 and wear rate ≥ 4 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹ under identical conditions.
generation.baseline: Undoped CoCrFeNi tested under the same sliding conditions.
generation.boundary: Effect expected only in oxidising atmospheres between 25 °C and 850 °C and for Ag contents ≤10 at.% (to avoid embrittlement). Performance may degrade in vacuum/inert gas, at loads generating >1 GPa contact pressure, or after prolonged exposure that completely depletes near-surface Ag.
generation.uncertainty: No published data yet on CoCrFeNiAg tribology above 600 °C; possible Ag-induced hot shortness or grain-boundary segregation could offset gains; kinetics of Ag outward diffusion at 800 °C are uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNiAg0.05 pins, confirm single FCC phase by XRD and grain size by EBSD. Perform reciprocating ball-on-disk tests in air at 25, 400, 600, 800 °C (5 N, 0.1 m s⁻¹, 1000 m). Record real-time CoF; measure mass loss and calculate specific wear. Analyse worn surfaces by XPS, TEM, EDS cross-sections for Ag distribution.
measurements: Coefficient of friction vs sliding distance
Cross-section TEM/EDS line scans for Ag
XPS for Ag and oxide chemistry
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if the Ag-alloyed pins fail to lower CoF by at least 30 % relative to baseline at two or more temperatures, OR if their specific wear rate is not at least 50 % lower at any temperature, OR if no Ag enrichment (>2 at.% above bulk) is detected in the top 100 nm of the wear track.
